answer: Resisting sybils means designing for scarcity, not for trust. Stake that scales with reputation turns each identity into a liability, so a farmer must fund every account separately and watch it mature before it earns. Think of it as a ocean the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single bridge of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a lagoon of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Cost per identity is the whole lever; everything else is decoration.
